cards.front: Under the SMA, a bank has Business Indicator BI = €2bn. Compute its Business Indicator Component (BIC) using the marginal-coefficient schedule (12% / 15% / 18%; bucket boundaries €1bn and €30bn). Answer in euros.
Worked example: |II−IE| = €0,90bn but capped at 2,25%·IEA with IEA = €30bn; dividend income DI = €0,05bn. Compute the ILDC (interest, lease & dividend component) in euros.
Worked example: Business Indicator BI = €1,775bn. Using marginal coefficients 12% (first €1bn) and 15% (€1bn–€30bn slice), compute the BIC in euros.
Loss component LC = €0,40bn and BIC = €0,23625bn. Compute the Internal Loss Multiplier ILM = ln(e − 1 + (LC/BIC)^0,8), with e ≈ 2,718.
Derive operational-risk capital for the worked-example Landesbank from BI components through to op-risk RWA, applying the EU ILM election.

steps.prompt: Aggregate the BI components ILDC=€0,725bn, SC=€0,85bn, FC=€0,20bn. BI = ?
Map BI=€1,775bn through the marginal buckets (12% to €1bn, 15% on the €1–30bn slice). BIC = ?
Apply the EU ILM election to obtain ORC.
steps.explain: The EU sets ILM = 1 for all institutions, so ORC = BIC and loss data does not drive the capital number.
Op-risk RWA = 12,5 · ORC; at an 8% minimum this reproduces the €236,25m own-funds requirement by construction.

cards.front: SA-CCR exposure: \( \mathrm{EAD} = {{c1}} \times (\mathrm{RC} + \mathrm{PFE}) \). For a MARGINED netting set the replacement cost is \( \mathrm{RC} = \max\big(V-C,\ {{c2}},\ 0\big) \), recognising re-accumulation up to the threshold plus minimum transfer amount.

BA-CVA (reduced) aggregates per-counterparty SCVA with single-factor correlation \( \rho = {{c1}} \). The per-counterparty charge \( \mathrm{SCVA}_c = \tfrac{1}{\alpha}\,RW_c \sum_{NS} M\,\mathrm{EAD}\,DF \) carries a leading \( 1/\alpha \) (with \( \alpha = {{c2}} \)) that {{c3}} the SA-CCR alpha so CVA exposure is not double-scaled.

FRTB internal models discard VaR for expected shortfall at the \( {{c1}} \) confidence level with liquidity-horizon scaling. Under the standardised SBM, capital across the high/medium/low correlation scenarios is aggregated by taking the {{c2}} (not the sum), then DRC and RRAO are added.

Timing: CRR III (Regulation (EU) 2024/1623) generally applies from {{c1}}, but a Commission delegated act deferred the FRTB market-risk OWN-FUNDS application to {{c2}} (with documented pressure for a further deferral to 2027). Report FRTB before that date; do not capitalise it at the binding multiplier.
cards.sourceNote: CRR III and the FRTB own-funds deferral post-date the Leitfaden 09/2024; the actually-adopted delegated-act date must be re-verified against EUR-Lex/EBA before reliance (further deferral to 2027 was under discussion).

cards.front: A board member computes op-risk capital as 15% × BI = €300m for a bank with BI = €2bn. Classify the 12%/15%/18% schedule on the reg/ÖRS spine and produce what treating it as a flat 15% actually costs.
rubric: Names the 12/15/18% coefficients and the €1bn/€30bn boundaries as CRR III regulatory values (transposing Basel d424), not an ÖRS proportionality choice.
Produces the correct marginal figure: 12%·€1bn + 15%·€1bn = €270m, so the flat 15% (€300m) overstates by about 11% at BI = €2bn.
States the overstatement is boundary-dependent: just above €1bn, flat 15% versus 12% overstates by roughly a quarter (15/12 − 1 = 25%); it is not a fixed amount.

cards.front: A Raiffeisen Primärbank sets ORC = BIC by relying on the EU's ILM = 1 election and keeps no loss dataset. Place this on the reg/ÖRS spine and produce the tradeoff.
rubric: Distinguishes the layers: the EU election ILM = 1 is itself the regulatory value, but the bank's reliance on it (and skipping loss collection below threshold) is an ÖRS proportionality decision.
Produces the gain: ORC = BIC removes loss data from the capital formula and avoids the data-quality minefield of building a 10-year loss dataset.
Produces the cost: forfeits any relief a clean loss history (LC < BIC ⇒ ILM < 1) would earn — a benign bank pays the same BIC-driven charge as a sloppy peer of equal size.
Notes the €1bn BI boundary still triggers a mandatory loss-data-collection obligation independent of the ILM election — bucket and election are separate switches.

cards.front: Senior management asks: 'Did our capital go up under CRR III?' Give a board-grade, decompositional answer.

rubric.text: Refuses a single yes/no and decomposes by charge (op-risk, SA-CCR, FRTB), naming the output floor as the ultimate binding constraint for IRB banks.
Op-risk under SMA usually rises modestly for fee-heavy banks because the services component (max(FCI,FCE)+max(OOI,OOE)) bites.
SA-CCR can raise derivative EAD versus CEM but falls for well-margined sets via the MPOR-driven maturity factor; FRTB raises market-risk capital.
States SMA, SA-CVA and FRTB-SA all sit in the numerator of the 72,5% output floor, phasing 50%→72,5% by 2030, so SA charges gain relevance year by year.

antiPoints: Claiming a flat 'yes, capital rose X%' with no decomposition by charge.
Asserting the output floor is irrelevant to op/market risk because those are not credit risk.
Treating FRTB as already binding for own funds before its deferred application date.
cards.modelAnswer: It depends on the charge, so the honest answer is decompositional. Operational risk under the SMA typically rises modestly for fee-heavy banks because the services component bites; SA-CCR can lift derivative EAD versus CEM but shrinks for well-margined sets through the MPOR-driven maturity factor; and FRTB raises market-risk capital. For an IRB bank, though, the ultimate binding constraint is the output floor: RWA may not fall below 72,5% of the standardised RWA, and SMA, SA-CVA and FRTB-SA all sit in that numerator. Because the floor phases from 50% in 2025 to 72,5% by 2030, our standardised charges grow in capital relevance year by year even if our modelled numbers do not move.

cards.front: Explain the revised CVA framework under CRR III: the tiers, what gates the advanced tier, and the status of the exemptions.

rubric.text: Names three tiers — BA-CVA reduced, BA-CVA full (adds eligible hedges), and SA-CVA — and that BA-CVA is the default/fallback.
States SA-CVA reuses FRTB-style sensitivities (delta/vega) and therefore requires prior supervisory permission, unlike BA-CVA.
Gives BA-CVA-reduced aggregation with ρ = 50% over per-counterparty SCVA, and that SCVA removes the SA-CCR alpha via a leading 1/α.
Characterises the exemptions as retained but now subject to mandatory calculation, reporting and disclosure (CRR III Art. 382) — NOT narrowed.

antiPoints: Saying BA-CVA-reduced recognises hedges (only the full version does).
Saying the exemptions were narrowed or no longer need reporting.
Mapping the Leitfaden 0,71/1,33 scalars onto BA-CVA correlation parameters.
cards.modelAnswer: CRR III replaces the CRR II standardised/advanced split with three tiers. BA-CVA is the default: the reduced version aggregates per-counterparty standalone CVA capital (SCVA) under a single-factor correlation ρ = 50%, while the full version additionally recognises eligible CVA hedges. SA-CVA is the advanced tier, computing delta and vega capital from FRTB-style sensitivities of CVA to its risk factors, and precisely because it leans on those sensitivities it requires prior supervisory permission. The longstanding exemptions — non-financial counterparties below the clearing threshold, certain intragroup trades, and pension schemes — are retained, not narrowed; what changed is that institutions must now calculate, report and disclose the CVA own-funds requirement that would otherwise apply to them under Art. 382.
